ideas.title: Approval Queue: nothing goes out without you
ideas.hook: Your AI agents draft real work, and you clear it all in one calm inbox with one tap: Send it, Fix it, Not this.
ideas.why: Anthropic's Claude for Small Business (May 2026) and Gusto's AI teammate both lead with approvals, and owners on Indie Hackers say they want an approval list before anything is sent. The 100-person test backed it 67 for, 12 against, 21 undecided, with the condition that it takes one tap and drafts are specific.
ideas.script: What it does: each office gets an Approvals inbox. When the team briefing runs, agents also write 3-6 finished drafts (a customer reply, a price change, a post) based on the company description and live Shopify or Stripe stats. Screen: a new Approvals section inside the office, plus a line at the top of the Morning Brief ('4 things waiting for you'). The owner taps Send it, Fix it (edit inline, then approve) or Not this (one-line reason). Approve all low-risk handles internal and public items; money and customer items always need a tap. Nothing is sent for real yet, so Send it marks approved and offers Copy and Mark as sent. Data: a new ApprovalItem entity (plan_id, agent_name, kind, risk, title, draft, why, status, edited_draft, skip_reason, decided_at) and a decision log with CSV export. Pricing: Free sees 3 items a week, paid tiers see all, so safety is never paywalled. Two-week check: share of drafts approved within 24h (target 60%+), daily opens of Approvals, and Free-to-paid conversions after hitting the cap. Risks: it becomes a graveyard if it nags or drafts are generic; competitors can copy the buttons, so draft quality is the moat.
ideas.buildPrompt:
Paste into Omar's Main Chat in the Claude app.

Use the Base44 connector on Growth Architect (app id 699b4057d65174480989a52e). First read these files: src/pages/Office.jsx, src/components/hq/Tasks.jsx, src/components/hq/useBriefing.js, src/components/hq/shared.jsx, base44/functions/teamBriefing, base44/entities/CompanyTask.jsonc and src/data/pricing.js. Then create a checkpoint, then build the change by editing the app's files directly.

Build an "Approval Queue" for each office (company). Promise on screen: "Nothing goes out without you."

1) New entity ApprovalItem: plan_id, agent_name, kind (reply, price_change, post, email, task), risk (money, customer, public, internal), title, draft, why (one plain sentence on what the agent saw), status (pending, approved, edited, skipped), edited_draft, skip_reason, decided_at. Same row-level rules as CompanyTask (only the creator reads and writes).

2) Extend the teamBriefing backend function so that besides notes and tasks it also writes 3 to 6 ApprovalItem rows, each a finished draft grounded in the company's real description and live DataSource stats (for example a customer reply, a price change, a social post). Reuse the existing AI call pattern in that function. Do not add new credit costs; it runs inside the existing team briefing.

3) New "Approvals" section inside the office (not a left sidebar, not a new top-level page): a calm inbox grouped by agent, each card showing the title, the draft, the "why" line and three buttons: "Send it", "Fix it" (inline edit then approve) and "Not this" (asks for a one-line reason). Add "Approve all low-risk" for internal and public items only. Money and customer items always need their own tap. Because nothing is connected to a real sending service yet, "Send it" marks the item approved and shows "Copy" plus "Mark as sent". Do not pretend anything was sent.

4) Morning Brief: lead with "N things waiting for you" linking to Approvals. One daily digest only, no repeated pings. Add a weekly recap line: "You approved X things this week."

5) Tiers: Free sees 3 pending items per week and a quiet "N more waiting, upgrade to see them" line. Paid tiers see everything. Update TIER_FEATURES in pricing.js accordingly. Do not paywall the Skip button.

6) Add a "Decision log" tab listing every decision by agent with a CSV export.

Rules to repeat: keep the Stripe integration exactly as it is; keep the professional look (no bright "dopamine" styling); connections and settings belong to each office; no left sidebar.

Finish line: with a test company the briefing creates items, Send it, Fix it and Not this all work and persist after refresh, the Free cap shows correctly, and the Morning Brief links to Approvals. Test it in the preview with show_app_preview, then report what changed.

swarm.idea: Approval Queue: nothing goes out without you
swarm.verdict: Most people would back it: 'nothing goes out without you' is the trust story, but only if it takes one tap and the drafts are specific, not generic.

groups.name: Small-business owners
groups.quote: I let an AI answer one customer and it quoted the wrong price. A one-tap approve before anything goes out is the only way I'd connect my email.

groups.name: Growth Architect customers
groups.quote: I'd pay Pro for the 'nothing goes out without you' promise alone. It's what lets me connect my email.

groups.name: Skeptics
groups.quote: It's a table in a database with a status column. I could build that in a weekend. The value is entirely whether the drafts are good.

groups.name: Marketers and agencies
groups.quote: Okay, batch approve plus a client-shareable queue changes my read. I'd test it for two clients. Graveyard risk stays if the brief doesn't nag.

groups.name: Investors and SaaS founders
groups.quote: As a buyer: trust is the sale. Letting a small-business owner say 'it only does what I approve' beats every feature list.

topPraise: 'Nothing goes out without you' is a clear trust promise that lets owners connect email and shops
The decision log works as an audit trail
Morning brief that says '4 waiting' gives a daily reason to open the app
topObjections: Approval inboxes become graveyards if it takes more than a tap or pings all day
Generic drafts stay generic with an Approve button on them
Not a moat: competitors ship approvals too, and a queue is easy to copy
swarm.changedMinds: Batch approve and a rules layer ('always ask on money and refunds, auto-send FAQ replies') moved several against voices to undecided or for; a free taste of 3 items a week answered the paywall complaint.
fixes: Add one-tap Approve all for low-risk items, plus one digest per day instead of many pings
Keep money items (prices, refunds) always in the queue, and let Free users see 3 items a week so safety is not paywalled
Show a real sample draft with real numbers on the page, and record a reason when someone skips so drafts improve
swarm.limits: One model played all 100 invented agents (82 spoke or voted; 18 silent ones are counted at their seeded lean), so this is a rehearsal, not a forecast.

ideas.title: Landing page: one business, one clear price
ideas.hook: A marketing plan about your business, not everyone's.
ideas.why: Competitor lesson (Beat): Venturekit's 39% one-star reviews are about generic plans and surprise billing, and MarketingGuide AI's $49.99 per project has no reviews yet, so the first screen should show a named-business plan and a clear price.
ideas.script:
HEADLINE
A marketing plan about your business, not everyone's.

SUBHEAD
Tell Growth Architect what you sell, who you're after and what you can spend. You get a step-by-step plan, a budget tracker, a calendar for your phone and a PDF to keep.

WHAT YOU GET (one line each)
- Step-by-step guidance, so you know what to do first
- Budget tracker, so spend doesn't drift
- Calendar you can export to any calendar app
- Full plan as a PDF
- YouTube videos and studies picked for where to start
- A 100-person market test before you spend a dollar
- Pro: a daily competitor watch

PRICE LINE (put it above the button)
[fill in: your real price]. [fill in: only if true: Cancel any time.] No surprise annual charge. [fill in: only if true]

COMPARISON BLOCK
Business-plan tools are built for lenders and investors. This one is for the next 90 days of getting customers.

PROOF BLOCK
[fill in: one real sample plan, for example a home bakery, shown as a screenshot with the business named]

WHY THIS COPY
Venturekit's Trustpilot page (3.8/5, 107 reviews, 39% one-star) is mostly surprise billing, unanswered cancellations and 'generic' plans. MarketingGuide AI charges $49.99 per project and has 0 Capterra reviews. Predis.ai reviewers complain about generic visuals. Answer those three on the first screen: named business, clear price, steps.

ideas.title: AI Marketing Campaign Builder with Approval Workflow
ideas.hook: Generate multi-channel marketing campaigns in minutes, with full control over every piece of content.
ideas.why: Competitors like Shopify's Campaign Autopilot are implementing approval rules, and user complaints consistently highlight the need for human oversight to prevent generic content and 'hallucinations'. The 100-person test showed strong support for this feature, emphasizing time-saving and quality control.
ideas.script: This upgrade adds a 'Campaigns' section to the Growth Architect office. Users click 'New Campaign' and fill a simple form (product, promotion, target audience, dates). AI agents then generate drafts for social media posts (e.g., Instagram/Facebook captions, hashtags), email newsletters (subject line, body), and ad copy (variations for Google/Meta). All generated content appears in a centralized 'Approval Queue' dashboard. Each item can be previewed, edited in-app, approved, or rejected. Approving moves it to a 'Scheduled' or 'Exported' status, while rejecting allows for feedback to refine future AI output. This feature is for the Pro tier ($19.99/month). Success can be measured in 2 weeks by user engagement with the 'Campaigns' module, number of approved campaigns, and feedback on content quality. Risk: Initial AI output might still be generic, requiring user patience for the AI to learn.
ideas.buildPrompt:
Paste into Omar's Main Chat in the Claude app.

Use the Base44 connector on Growth Architect (app id 699b4057d65174480989a52e). First read the relevant files, specifically existing UI components for dashboards and forms, and create a checkpoint. Then build the change by editing the app's files directly.

Create a new 'Campaigns' section accessible from the main office interface, perhaps as a new 'floor' or a distinct 'department' within the existing 'Agents' tab. This section will contain two primary views:

1.  **New Campaign Form:** A user-friendly form to initiate a campaign. This form should capture:
    *   `Campaign Name` (text input)
    *   `Product/Promotion Details` (large text area, e.g., 'New collection of sustainable Islamic art prints, launching next month, target audience: eco-conscious Muslims aged 25-45')
    *   `Key Message/Goal` (text input, e.g., 'Increase pre-orders by 15%')
    *   `Start Date` and `End Date` (date pickers)
    *   A 'Generate Campaign' button.

2.  **Approval Queue Dashboard:** This dashboard will display all AI-generated content drafts. Each draft should be presented as a card or row, showing:
    *   `Content Type` (e.g., 'Instagram Post', 'Email Newsletter', 'Meta Ad Copy')
    *   A truncated `Content Preview` (full content viewable on click).
    *   `Channel` (e.g., 'Instagram', 'Email', 'Meta Ads').
    *   Three action buttons: 'Edit' (opens an in-app text editor for the content), 'Approve' (changes status to 'Approved'), and 'Reject' (changes status to 'Rejected', and prompts for a brief feedback input to guide the AI).

Implement an underlying entity schema for `Campaigns` and `CampaignAssets` to store the campaign brief, generated content, approval status, and user feedback. The AI agent logic (using Gemini) will take the campaign brief, generate content for social media (e.g., 3 variations of captions with relevant hashtags), email (subject line, body), and ad copy (e.g., 2 variations of headlines/descriptions). The system must learn from user edits and rejections to refine its generation for future campaigns, adapting to the user's specific brand voice and preferences.

Keep the Stripe integration exactly as it is; keep the professional look (no bright 'dopamine' styling); connections and settings belong to each office; no left sidebar. This feature will be available for Growth Architect's Pro tier ($19.99/month).

What must work: Users can create a campaign, view generated content, edit, approve, or reject it. The AI should show improvement over time based on feedback. How to test it in the preview: Create a sample campaign, review the generated content, make edits, and approve some items. Verify the status changes correctly. Report what files and components were added or changed.

swarm.idea: AI Marketing Campaign Builder with Approval Workflow
swarm.verdict: People would strongly back this if it genuinely saves time, ensures brand voice through the approval queue, and the AI learns effectively from feedback.

groups.name: Small Business Owners
groups.quote: This is exactly what I need. I spend hours trying to come up with content for different platforms. If this gives me drafts I can quickly approve, it's a huge time-saver.

groups.name: Current/Likely Growth Architect Customers
groups.quote: The approval queue is critical. I trust AI for ideas, but not for final output. This combines the best of both worlds – speed and control.

groups.name: Skeptics who tried AI tools that disappointed them
groups.quote: My main concern with AI has always been generic, templated content. If the editing and learning aspect truly works, and I have final say, this could be different.

groups.name: Marketers/Agency People
groups.quote: For small e-commerce clients, this is a scalable way to produce consistent, multi-channel content without needing a huge team. The approval workflow is a smart move.

groups.name: Investors/SaaS Founders
groups.quote: This addresses a clear market need: efficient content creation with quality control for SMBs. The learning feedback loop is a strong retention driver. Pricing model needs to be clear.

topPraise: Massive time savings on content creation across multiple channels.
The approval queue ensures brand voice consistency and prevents errors.
The AI learning from edits is a key differentiator and builds trust.
Streamlines marketing efforts from a single brief, making campaigns more cohesive.
topObjections: Initial AI output might still be too generic, requiring significant edits.
Desire for more direct publishing integrations to social media/email platforms.
Concerns about over-reliance on AI potentially stifling human creativity.
swarm.changedMinds: The emphasis on the one-tap approval queue and the AI's ability to learn from user edits and rejections significantly swayed skeptics who previously found AI content generic or untrustworthy.
fixes: Clearly communicate that the AI improves over time with user feedback.
Prioritize integrations for direct publishing to popular social media platforms and email services.
Offer templates or guides to help users provide more specific campaign briefs for better initial AI output.

items.title: Shopify Sidekick: AI Assistant
items.creator: Shopify
items.whyItWorks: Offers a wide range of AI-powered tasks directly within the Shopify ecosystem, leveraging existing user base. Its convenience is a major draw for Shopify merchants.
items.lessonForUs: While free and integrated, Sidekick can be generic. Growth Architect can win by specializing in *marketing strategy and execution* with more reliable, specific plans for e-commerce.

items.title: Gorgias AI: Customer Service Helpdesk
items.creator: Gorgias
items.whyItWorks: Deep Shopify integration for customer service, resolving common queries across channels. The core helpdesk is valuable.
items.lessonForUs: The unpredictable, escalating pricing of Gorgias AI is a significant pain point. Growth Architect should emphasize a *clear, flat monthly fee* to attract small businesses seeking budget stability.

items.title: Klaviyo AI: Email & SMS Marketing Automation
items.creator: Klaviyo
items.metric: Pricing scales rapidly with contact list size
items.whyItWorks: Powerful marketing automation, segmentation, and content generation for e-commerce. Strong Shopify integration.
items.lessonForUs: Klaviyo's pricing model, especially for its AI add-ons, can quickly become expensive for growing stores. Growth Architect can differentiate with *transparent, predictable pricing* that doesn't punish success.

items.title: Molin AI: AI Shopping Assistant
items.creator: Molin AI
items.whyItWorks: Specialized AI for shopping assistance, product recommendations, and support, built natively for Shopify and other platforms. Accessible pricing.
items.lessonForUs: Focus on specific, revenue-driving AI agents (like product recommendation or support) that integrate well. Growth Architect's 'office of agents' can cover these areas with a unified approach.

items.title: Rep AI: Agentic Commerce OS
items.creator: Rep AI
items.metric: G2 4.9/5 (62 reviews), Shopify App Store 4.7/5 (111 reviews)
items.whyItWorks: Proactively engages shoppers, detects hesitation, and boosts conversion/AOV. Strong positive reviews indicate real value.
items.lessonForUs: Positive reviews for proactive engagement show the value of AI agents that *act*. Growth Architect's 'nothing sends without approval' combined with proactive suggestions can be a strong trust point.

items.title: Tidio (Lyro AI): Customer Communication
items.creator: Tidio
items.whyItWorks: Integrates live chat, AI chatbot (Lyro), and help desk with accessible pricing and Shopify integration. Solves common support queries.
items.lessonForUs: High review counts on Shopify App Store indicate strong market penetration for integrated support solutions. Growth Architect needs clear value proposition for its marketing agents over support-focused ones.

items.title: Zipchat AI: Cart Recovery & Proactive Support
items.creator: Zipchat AI
items.whyItWorks: AI-native, trains on live product catalogs, focuses on revenue generation through cart recovery (WhatsApp) and proactive outreach. Quick setup.
items.lessonForUs: Specific, high-impact revenue metrics (cart recovery) are powerful. Growth Architect can show how its marketing plans directly lead to measurable outcomes like increased sales or reduced abandoned carts.

items.title: How I'd get my first 100 customers with a Shopify store - 2026 Guide
items.creator: Louis Cook (YouTube)
items.whyItWorks: Emphasizes defining ideal customer and crafting compelling offers. Real-world advice for beginners.
items.lessonForUs: Content about 'how to get first customers' is evergreen. Growth Architect can frame its output as the 'playbook' for this, showing how its agents help define customers and offers.

competitors.lessonForUs: Like Gorgias, Klaviyo's pricing scales rapidly and unpredictably with usage/contacts. Growth Architect can differentiate with *transparent, predictable pricing* that doesn't punish success.

competitors.oneLiner: AI business plan, forecast and pitch-deck generator with a free tier and paid unlocks.
competitors.price: Free tier; reviewers mention surprise annual charges
competitors.contentStrategy: Directory listings (Futurepedia, G2 AI, B12) rather than its own social content, as far as this run could find.
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library, TikTok Creative Center and LinkedIn Ad Library weren't reachable from this run's tools, so no live ads could be confirmed.
competitors.howTheyGrew: Free plan as the hook, then paid unlocks. Trustpilot is 3.8/5 on 107 reviews (20 in the last 12 months) with 39% one-star. A 26 Mar 2026 one-star is still about an unexpected annual charge; others cite generic plans, unanswered cancellation emails and PDF exports that cut off graphs. The company has not responded to negative reviews.
competitors.lessonForUs: Billing and 'generic plan' are still the top complaints a year on. Growth Architect should emphasize 'one specific plan for *your* business, clear price, cancel any time' (only if true) in the first screen of the site and in promos.

competitors.name: MarketingGuide AI
competitors.oneLiner: AI marketing plan generator (plans, personas, email sequences) for freelancers and small businesses. The closest direct match to Growth Architect.
competitors.price: One-time: $49.99 for 1 project, $99.99 for 5, $199.99 for 10; no free trial
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library, TikTok Creative Center and LinkedIn Ad Library weren't reachable from this run's tools, so no live ads could be confirmed.
competitors.howTheyGrew: Still 0 reviews on Capterra. Pitches 15 documents per project (plan, personas, email sequences, social plan) with PDF/DOCX export. No visible content or ads.
competitors.lessonForUs: Its price per project is high. Growth Architect's step-by-step guide, budget tracker, calendar, and PDF export can be framed as 'more than a one-off document, for less than $49.99 a month' once Omar confirms his pricing offers continuous value.

competitors.name: Template.net AI Marketing Plan
competitors.oneLiner: Free AI marketing plan generator inside Template.net, for marketers, freelancers and startups.
competitors.price: Page says '100% free', no sign-up needed (limits not stated)
competitors.contentStrategy: Free tool as a lead magnet for its template library. No short-form content found.
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library, TikTok Creative Center and LinkedIn Ad Library weren't reachable from this run's tools, so no live ads could be confirmed.
competitors.howTheyGrew: Free, instant, no sign-up; outputs an editable plan with goals, audience, channels, budget and timeline, exportable to DOCX/PDF and shareable by link or QR. It cites no user counts or reviews.
competitors.lessonForUs: The free no-sign-up generator is the real price anchor for 'marketing plan' searches. Growth Architect can't beat free on price, so beat it on follow-through: budget tracker, calendar export and the 100-person market test (referring to the previous brief's finding).

swarms.idea: AI Marketing Campaign Builder with Approval Workflow
swarms.verdict: People would strongly back this if it genuinely saves time, ensures brand voice through the approval queue, and the AI learns effectively from feedback.

groups.name: Small Business Owners
groups.quote: This is exactly what I need. I spend hours trying to come up with content for different platforms. If this gives me drafts I can quickly approve, it's a huge time-saver.

groups.name: Current/Likely Growth Architect Customers
groups.quote: The approval queue is critical. I trust AI for ideas, but not for final output. This combines the best of both worlds – speed and control.

groups.name: Skeptics who tried AI tools that disappointed them
groups.quote: My main concern with AI has always been generic, templated content. If the editing and learning aspect truly works, and I have final say, this could be different.

groups.name: Marketers/Agency People
groups.quote: For small e-commerce clients, this is a scalable way to produce consistent, multi-channel content without needing a huge team. The approval workflow is a smart move.

groups.name: Investors/SaaS Founders
groups.quote: This addresses a clear market need: efficient content creation with quality control for SMBs. The learning feedback loop is a strong retention driver. Pricing model needs to be clear.

topPraise: Massive time savings on content creation across multiple channels.
The approval queue ensures brand voice consistency and prevents errors.
The AI learning from edits is a key differentiator and builds trust.
Streamlines marketing efforts from a single brief, making campaigns more cohesive.
topObjections: Initial AI output might still be too generic, requiring significant edits.
Desire for more direct publishing integrations to social media/email platforms.
Concerns about over-reliance on AI potentially stifling human creativity.
swarms.changedMinds: The emphasis on the one-tap approval queue and the AI's ability to learn from user edits and rejections significantly swayed skeptics who previously found AI content generic or untrustworthy.
fixes: Clearly communicate that the AI improves over time with user feedback.
Prioritize integrations for direct publishing to popular social media platforms and email services.
Offer templates or guides to help users provide more specific campaign briefs for better initial AI output.
swarms.limits: one model played all 100 agents; this is a rehearsal, not a forecast

swarms.idea: Approval Queue: nothing goes out without you
swarms.verdict: Most people would back it: 'nothing goes out without you' is the trust story, but only if it takes one tap and the drafts are specific, not generic.

groups.name: Small-business owners
groups.quote: I let an AI answer one customer and it quoted the wrong price. A one-tap approve before anything goes out is the only way I'd connect my email.

groups.name: Growth Architect customers
groups.quote: I'd pay Pro for the 'nothing goes out without you' promise alone. It's what lets me connect my email.

groups.name: Skeptics
groups.quote: It's a table in a database with a status column. I could build that in a weekend. The value is entirely whether the drafts are good.

groups.name: Marketers and agencies
groups.quote: Okay, batch approve plus a client-shareable queue changes my read. I'd test it for two clients. Graveyard risk stays if the brief doesn't nag.

groups.name: Investors and SaaS founders
groups.quote: As a buyer: trust is the sale. Letting a small-business owner say 'it only does what I approve' beats every feature list.

topPraise: 'Nothing goes out without you' is a clear trust promise that lets owners connect email and shops
The decision log works as an audit trail
Morning brief that says '4 waiting' gives a daily reason to open the app
topObjections: Approval inboxes become graveyards if it takes more than a tap or pings all day
Generic drafts stay generic with an Approve button on them
Not a moat: competitors ship approvals too, and a queue is easy to copy
swarms.changedMinds: Batch approve and a rules layer ('always ask on money and refunds, auto-send FAQ replies') moved several against voices to undecided or for; a free taste of 3 items a week answered the paywall complaint.
fixes: Add one-tap Approve all for low-risk items, plus one digest per day instead of many pings
Keep money items (prices, refunds) always in the queue, and let Free users see 3 items a week so safety is not paywalled
Show a real sample draft with real numbers on the page, and record a reason when someone skips so drafts improve
swarms.limits: One model played all 100 invented agents (82 spoke or voted; 18 silent ones are counted at their seeded lean), so this is a rehearsal, not a forecast.
